name: A House Divided and Remade
description: Cotton, conscience and conflict: how slavery split the United States, how the Civil War was fought and won, and how Reconstruction tried to remake the reunited country.

checkpoints.name: Cotton and chains
checkpoints.note: The cotton gin makes slave-grown cotton hugely profitable and, although the US bans importing enslaved people in 1808, ties the South to slavery and a vast internal slave trade. Frederick Douglass, who escaped slavery, becomes its fiercest critic, and Harriet Beecher Stowe's Uncle Tom's Cabin turns the issue into a national cause.

checkpoints.name: The road to war
checkpoints.note: The new Republican Party opposes the spread of slavery, John Brown's raid terrifies the South, and the election of Abraham Lincoln leads Southern states to leave the Union.

checkpoints.name: The war
checkpoints.note: The Confederate States fight the Union. Robert E. Lee leads the main Confederate army and Ulysses S. Grant rises to command the Union's. The ironclad USS Monitor and the first Gatling guns show a new kind of war, Gettysburg turns the tide, the Emancipation Proclamation and the Gettysburg Address give the war a new purpose, and the Thirteenth Amendment ends slavery.

checkpoints.name: Reconstruction
checkpoints.note: Reconstruction tries to give freed people citizenship through the Fourteenth Amendment, while the Ku Klux Klan answers with terror. Walt Whitman mourns the war's dead, Grant is elected president in 1868, the transcontinental railroad joins the reunited country in 1869, and Reconstruction ends in 1877 when federal troops leave the South.
